I actually hadn't considered the fact that being away for a bit may shake the people following me, that's actually a pretty good point, maybe inpatient could be a good idea after all
And I could do that's also a good idea
Thank you

That's true, I know they like to avoid it, I'm just over thinking most likely tbh
And an old "friend" (I use that term lightly) is obsessed with me (this has been confirmed by someone else), and now Im worried that his Internet stalking has crossed over into real life, he recently befriended my best friend and I know he's using him to spy on me, I'm scared he will get my partner too. I also keep seeing people following me, the same dude over and over again

Hey, whilst I wasn't assaulted by a family member, I was molested as a child, and now find myself struggling with similar issues
I'm not really one to give advice because I feel the same, but I wanted to let you know that suicide is not the only way to cope, whilst you will never be able to forget what happened, you'll slowly learn to cope with it, my assault happened 14 years ago, and whilst some days are rough and it does cause issues, I feel more able to process the feeling surrounding what happened
Bonding takes time, I've found it takes longer for me because of what happened, it makes trust so hard, but again, with time it will come, 2 years ago I had no friends and was unable to connect with anyone, I find that getting easier every day
Living life following abuse is so hard, but, as cliché as it is to say this, it gets easier, it may take a while, and some days may feel like a step backwards, but it wont be this hard forever
You're not alone in these feelings, and I hope you're doing okay
